THE LAST LIGHT

One last scene.

EXT. FRONT DOOR — EVENING

She reaches the step. A light is on inside.

For a moment, she holds the key above the lock.

A bus passes behind her. We cut to the street.

There is no one at the door.

END
MirReady

Does the cut still leave her choice open?

Yes. We leave before she acts, as you asked in the earlier note.

The empty doorway may imply she left. Worth testing that ambiguity.

STARTING POINT

Precise frame.
Unpredictable body.

Not a synth skin. Four ways to give expressive motion a bounded job, while keeping words, controls and evidence still.

01 / APERTURE

The everyday interface.

Best balance of character and concentration. Start here for the main app.

Risk: a fluid orb can feel like generic AI decoration. Keep it small, state-bound and optional.

02 / IMPRINT

Memory you can read.

A record-first view with authorship, corrections and selected context.

Risk: material richness cannot substitute for good search. The text must do the retrieval.

03 / PATCH

Choose what comes in.

A deliberate workspace for composing a limited source set before a turn.

Risk: merging forms may imply agreement. Keep source boundaries and labels visible.

04 / SIDECAR

Less app. More work.

A compact companion beside a document rather than another full-screen destination.

Risk: a narrow window hides context. Sources need an easy expansion.

The two boards, in conversation.

Selected references from the saved 144-image collection. IDs follow the existing study. These are design readings, not technical evidence.

What this study does—and does not—claim.

The saved roster, prior image-specific readings, product brief and V11 documentation were read. Thumbnail and board images were recovered, but the image tools returned filenames rather than viewable pixels in this pass. This is a provisional synthesis from those readings, not a fresh full-board visual audit or a verified viewing of the video. The live boards were not exhaustively refreshed.

All four layouts are proposals. Conversations, dates, files and behavior are fictional, local demonstrations. No model calls, account changes, microphone access, telemetry or private conversations are used.

Existing product controls informed the studies: composer, attachments, model selection, files and tasks. The record browser, correction layer, context desk and sidecar arrangement are proposed extensions. Model changes here affect the next simulated turn; they do not prove cross-model identity or accuracy.

Cross-reading Hultén’s framed fluid + Julia’s porthole (036) + Chris’s glass-well widget (098).
